column1: # N1 vs N2 val series, the seed-only null pair (S285, S286).
# 'step' rows are train.py's periodic val: val_batches = 20 (train.py:408).
# 'final' rows are the epoch-end val: val_batches_full = 100 (train.py:409), the
# estimator the pre-registered criterion reads and the one train.py's own comment
# calls comparable across runs. The two columns are DIFFERENT estimators of the same
# quantity and their gaps differ by ~50%; that is S286.
# Extracted from the pod's runs/anneal_n1_0908.log and runs/anneal_n2_0908.log,
# which are pod-only and not in this repository (44's R10 finding on PR #117).
# EPOCH-END LINE, BOTH FIELDS. train.py's runlog prints `ep 1/1 train <t> val <v>`:
# val gap +0.048 (100 batches, the estimator the criterion reads).
# train gap -0.410 -- OPPOSITE SIGN AND 8.5x LARGER, from a seed-only pair. The train field is
# NOT an epoch mean: `last = loss.item() * Cfg.accum` is set on log steps only, so it is ONE
# MICRO-BATCH at the last log step. Two numbers on one line in the same units, and only one of
# them estimates anything. Do not compare the train field across runs.
